title: Stanislaus (11 April)
hookLine: a bishop of Kraków killed by the king he had rebuked

lines: WHEN A PASTOR TELLS POWER NO.
cards: A small church on a hill outside Kraków. A bishop is at the altar, saying Mass. The door opens, and armed men come in, sent by the king.
According to the tradition, they can't bring themselves to touch him. So the king walks in himself and strikes the bishop down at the altar. That's how the story is told in Poland.
The bishop's name was Stanislaus. The king's was Bolesław. And between them stands a question that keeps coming back: what happens when a pastor tells a powerful man no?

teach.b: Start with the sources, because they disagree. An early Polish chronicle is brief and harsh about him, and calls the bishop a traitor.

A later chronicler, himself a bishop of Kraków, tells it the other way: Stanislaus rebuked the king for cruelty and for his sins, the king wouldn't listen, and the bishop finally cut him off from the Church.
Historians still argue about what really happened. The sources do agree on the ending.

teach.h: THE KING KILLED HIM, THEN LOST HIS THRONE.
teach.b: The king had the bishop killed, and soon afterward the king himself was driven from his throne and died in exile.

teach.h: A SIGN FOR A DIVIDED COUNTRY.
teach.b: Tradition adds more: a dead man raised to testify for the bishop in a land dispute, and the bishop's scattered body growing whole again, which Poles later read as a picture of their divided country one day becoming one.
The Church named Stanislaus a saint, and he became a patron of Poland. His story echoes an older one.

teach.h: IT IS NOT LAWFUL FOR THEE.
teach.b: In the Gospel of Mark, John the Baptist tells King Herod, in the Douay-Rheims: "It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife." John lost his head for that sentence.

In Polish memory, Stanislaus became a sign that the Church's voice belongs to the people, not to the throne. A later bishop of Kraków, Karol Wojtyła, who became Pope John Paul the Second, kept returning to him.
The bishop of Kraków is a title with a memory.

how: Catholics keep Stanislaus's memorial on 11 April; in Poland his feast is kept in May with a procession in Kraków, carrying his relics from Wawel Cathedral to the church on the Skałka hill.

games.q: you're the bishop of Kraków. the king is cruel, and he has ignored your warnings. what do you do?
o: cut him off from the Church.
games.why: the later chronicle says he excommunicated the king, and the king had him killed. the older chronicle tells it differently.

practice: Bring Poland to mind as people, not a map: a grandmother in Kraków walking to morning Mass, a family who left and a family who stayed, Polish neighbors or coworkers where you live.

Hold the country's long memory of being divided, and whatever it carries today. If you pray, pray for Poland, perhaps with the Hail Mary or the Our Father; if you don't, hold its people in mind with good will.

wordCard.voice: Stanislaus. A bishop of Kraków killed at the king's order after he rebuked him, honored as a patron of Poland.
